title: El Hotel
scene: a six-storey hotel with the front wall removed: thirty rooms, twenty simultaneous lives, a lobby, a bar, a street
crowdRule: Every room is lit from within and the light temperature alternates warm/cool floor by floor; the wedding is lit warmer than its floor; the ground floor splits warm lobby / cool bar.
findIt: A black cat with pale eyes in eleven rooms, at eleven different heights (beds, sills, laps, tables, a bar stool).

readings.far: A cutaway hotel at night: dark frame, six bands of alternating warm and cool lit rooms, red canopy, yellow taxi, one pale line of water down the facade.
readings.middle: Thirty rooms with readable incidents (wedding, argument, burglary at an open window, overflowing bath, wake, party), a working lobby and bar, a roof with tank and laundry, and a leak running from the second floor to a puddle at the kerb.
readings.near: Figures with shoulders, hair and objects in hand; cats on sills and laps at eleven heights; puddle edges and wet reflections; bottles and bulbs at the bar.

techniques: six-storey cutaway grid, 6x5 rooms plus ground floor and roof
light-temperature alternation as the crowd rule
one continuous water leak crossing five floors
eleven repeated cats at eleven heights
wet-street reflections, canopy shadow, spill light
statement: A hotel is a machine for making strangers private in public, and the cutaway is the machine fantasy: every door open, every light on, no one speaking to anyone. The rule is the light - warm and cool alternating by floor - so the building reads as bands of living before it reads as people. The one line that crosses the floors is a leak, and the one thing that crosses the whole building is a cat.
